solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pigeon getting copper's helmet?

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the possessive ending gives its S
a helmet is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A bird somehow comes by a policeman's helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushat is a dialect name for the wood pigeon, a large wild dove.

clue.text: A husband that you might get after superior religious instruction!

definitions.text: A husband that you might get after superior religious instruction!

indicators.note: the A and H come after the other letters in the answer

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, superior
RI is the school subject Religious Instruction

explanation.surface: A schoolchild's Bible lesson introduces a famous husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a Bible lesson might well tell the story of Uriah the Hittite, Bathsheba's first husband, whom King David had killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Uriah the Hittite is the Old Testament husband of Bathsheba, a figure met in scripture lessons.

clue.text: Join up with the fellow, then yap freely inside

indicators.note: letters arranged freely are not kept in their order, so all are mixed together

parts.note: a fellow is a man, he
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to team up with a man and then chatter away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' is the anagram signal over all three parts; 'inside' is surface glue, picturing the chatter mixed in among the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To hyphenate words is to link them together with a short dash.

clue.text: Unproved statement in submission for PhD?

definitions.meaning: a proposition put forward to be argued or tested
the dissertation a doctoral candidate hands in

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a proposition to be argued and the long dissertation submitted for a doctorate.

clue.text: Power of tot — I walk all over the place

indicators.note: something all over the place is in disorder, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A toddler's strength as it staggers about everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is only a link word; the letters of TOT I WALK are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilowatt is a unit of power, a thousand watts.

clue.text: Calm down — I don't want to see that chest!

definitions.meaning: an idiom telling someone not to get angry

definitions.text: I don't want to see that chest!
definitions.meaning: taken literally, asking a man not to take his top off

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urges someone not to lose their temper, and literally asks a man to stay clothed above the waist.

clue.text: Wanting company to advance money, as you might say?

indicators.note: signals the letters are spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to loan some is to lend a little cash

explanation.surface: Someone lonely is willing to lend out cash, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loan some' said out loud matches a word meaning solitary.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling lonely means longing for companionship.

clue.text: I may be poured out by server at table

definitions.text: I may be poured out by server at table

indicators.note: the I is poured out of the server, so that letter goes

parts.note: a waiter serves at table

explanation.surface: The answer speaks: a waiter may pour me out at table.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's I is both the letter dropped and the answer talking, and a waiter does pour water at table.
explanation.definitionFit: A jug of tap water is commonly poured for diners by restaurant staff.

clue.text: A measure of Violet Elizabeth's malady?

indicators.note: Violet Elizabeth Bott lisps, so in her mouth an S becomes TH

parts.note: a malady is an illness, sickness

explanation.surface: How badly is a little girl ill?
explanation.walkthrough: Violet Elizabeth Bott is the lisping girl in Richmal Crompton's Just William books ("I'll thcream and thcream"), so her sickness comes out with TH for the first S.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth from one side to the other is a dimension one measures.

clue.text: Wife not sophisticated, wanting head covered — this cloth could hide it

indicators.note: lacking its head, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: something unsophisticated is simple

explanation.surface: A plain wife who wants her head covered might use this cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition is the head named earlier; 'covered' only links the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimple is a cloth headdress, as worn by nuns, covering head and neck.

clue.text: One German saint and one German genius

parts.note: ein is German for one
ein is German for one again

explanation.surface: A German saint and a German genius listed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, the physicist, is the archetypal brilliant mind.

clue.text: Church in weird style exhibiting happy-clappy mode?

parts.note: done in an uncanny way is done eerily

explanation.surface: A church with odd worship shows evangelical exuberance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happy-clappy' is a British dismissive term for lively evangelical worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in an upbeat, merry way is behaving with good spirits.

clue.text: Flier getting hit, needing hospital for short time

indicators.note: the hospital letter is put in place of the time letter

parts.note: to hit is to strike
T is short for time

explanation.surface: A pilot who was struck needs a brief hospital stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrike is a predatory songbird, so something that flies.

clue.text: A little drink knocked back in Italian city

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is turned round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a sip is a small mouthful of drink

explanation.surface: Downing a small drink in an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' sounds like gulping a drink but reverses A SIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisa, in Tuscany, is famous for its leaning tower.

clue.text: Nowadays Bradman's getting into fixed routine

indicators.note: says one piece goes inside the other
something fixed is repaired or rearranged, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the setter Bradman speaking of himself: I am, shortened to I'M

explanation.surface: These days the setter settles into a set routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' puts the setter's I'M inside INOURTE, which 'fixed' makes; setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means during the present era, in the current age.

clue.text: A Parisian maiden getting questioned becomes exposed

parts.note: un is French for a
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
to question is to ask

explanation.surface: A young French woman under interrogation finds herself laid bare.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, written M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unmasked means having one's disguise removed, so being revealed.

clue.text: Any rested drunk could be this

definitions.text: Any rested drunk could be this

indicators.note: something drunk is all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tipsy person who has rested would be sitting still.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: a drunk resting is inactive and seated.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedentary describes someone sitting a lot, inactive.

clue.text: Pack bananas as one of the ship's crew

parts.note: a pack of cards is a deck
a hand is a bunch of bananas

explanation.surface: Sailors loading fruit aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' suggests madness or an anagram, but a cluster of bananas is called a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckhand is a sailor doing manual work on board.

clue.text: In despair, having lost American Bob?

parts.note: Bob Hope was a famous American comedian
being without something is being less it

explanation.surface: Distraught at losing a US comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as without Bob Hope; the comedian's name supplies the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without any expectation of improvement means one is in despair.

clue.text: Parties needing hard cash

parts.note: dos are parties or celebrations
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Throwing parties takes ready money.
explanation.walkthrough: DOSH is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosh is informal slang for money.

clue.text: Two pages — second page gets looked at

parts.note: a text looked at has been read

explanation.surface: A magazine's double page gets its second look.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, two facing pages laid out as one are called a spread.

clue.text: Jeer, first off, showing spirit

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off

parts.note: to barrack is to jeer at a speaker or player

explanation.surface: Heckling first shows nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like courage, but it is a drink; 'first off' sounds like 'to begin with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrack is a strong liquor distilled in South Asia from palm sap or rice.

clue.text: A longing to be the leading character in horticulture

definitions.note: the first letter of that word, named as a letter

parts.note: an itch is a restless longing

explanation.surface: A gardener's yearning to lead the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the name of the letter that opens 'horticulture'.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter H is spelt out as a word, so it names the first letter there.

clue.text: One politician wanting harmony and protection

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an MP is a Member of Parliament
unity is harmony, agreement

explanation.surface: A lone politician seeks concord and security.
explanation.definitionFit: Impunity is exemption from punishment, a kind of shield from consequences.

clue.text: Celestial object — it turned brown

indicators.note: turned round, the word it is read backwards

parts.note: tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: A heavenly body that went brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned brown' reads as one phrase, but 'turned' reverses only IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Titan is the largest moon of Saturn, a body in space.

clue.text: Princess's characteristic to be absent- minded

parts.note: Di is Princess Diana
the possessive ending gives its S
a trait is a characteristic

explanation.surface: A princess is noted for being forgetful.
explanation.definitionFit: Distrait describes someone distracted, inattentive through worry.

clue.text: Demands of old lover met with deeds

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
deeds are acts

explanation.surface: A former partner's requests are answered with action.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact something is to insist on and obtain it, so a verb of requirement.

clue.text: Fish chaps brought to port — last of fish netted

indicators.note: a letter caught in a net is held inside, so it goes within the other letters

parts.note: chaps are men
Aden is a port in Yemen

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word fish

explanation.surface: Fishermen bring their catch into harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought to' is a charade link; 'netted' puts the H that 'last of' takes inside the rest. The first 'Fish' defines, the second supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The menhaden is an oily North American fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Milk business not excellent — if cows are this?

parts.note: dairying is the trade of producing milk
A1 means first-rate; written AI

explanation.surface: A dairy farm in decline as its herd stops yielding.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written as AI here: the digit 1 stands for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows that stop giving milk at the end of lactation are said to be going dry.
